mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns in inflation-up months are not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05), or CPIAUCSL remains below 0.3% for three consecutive months after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor compensation growth of at least 0.5% signals wage stickiness and labor market strength, which elevates expected corporate profits and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥ 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 24 months of PAYEMS ≥ 0.5% monthly growth, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05), or the correlation with labor cost growth falls below 0.2.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly expansion in HOUST retail sales exceeding 2% indicates resilient consumer demand, which lowers financing costs for firms and raises expected equity valuations, yielding positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 30 instances where HOUST > +2% MoM for two months, the 5-day forward return is negative on average (mean < 0), or the effect is not significant after controlling for lagged GDP growth (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO manufacturing index (≥ -1.5%) indicates supply-side pressures that raise uncertainty and compress margins, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by ≥ -1.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 40 instances of INDPRO contraction ≥ -1.5% MoM, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is explained by exchange rate movements (> 5% variance).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises above 5.0% for three consecutive months, the anticipation of higher borrowing costs suppresses risk appetite, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Across 12 windows of FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for three months, the 60-day forward return mean is not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is mediated by equity yield changes (< -0.2 pp).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 3.0% for two consecutive months reflects weak wage bargaining and reduced labor cost pressures, which lowers equity discount rates and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 3.0% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 30 such UNRATE < 3.0% windows, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly positive (mean ≤ 0), or the effect is not robust after controlling for GDP growth (F-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A double-digit monthly drop in RSAFS commercial loan demand signals a credit cycle contraction that raises perceived systemic risk, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by > -10% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: In 25 instances of RSAFS decline > -10% MoM, the 5-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (mean > -0.1), or the effect is driven by sector-specific shocks (> 40% of variance).

mechanism_narrative: When both INDPRO and GDPC1 show simultaneous contraction (INDPRO < 100 and GDPC1 < previous month) for two consecutive months, the dual supply shock elevates uncertainty and compresses earnings expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 AND GDPC1 < previous month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 30 such dual contraction events, the 20-day forward return mean is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05), or the effect is explained by commodity price movements (> 30% of variance).
